title: Full research pass review of the chaldean lane, 2026-10-19
semantics: Project-created review metadata. Versions include witnesses, components, translations and unresolved leads; their count is not a count of substantive revisions. Acquisition does not establish transcription, collation, normative revision or local reception. No ancestry is asserted.

review_files.storage: untracked workspace scratch; pinned here by SHA-256 only

uses.label: Chaldean Catholic Church
uses.finding: The Catholic book line is labelled from manuscript layers (Macomber's Chaldean manuscript tradition, including Vatican Syriac 491 of 1686, 44 of 1691, and 43, copied at Rome in 1701 by Patriarch Joseph I) through Rome 1767, a reported 1773 second edition, the Mosul 1900 three-volume lectionary set, the 1901 ordinary and proper, the 1936 Mosul reprint, the 1971 Baghdad first-anaphora Taksa, the 1982 Paris reprint with French translation, the 2005–2007 reform, the 2014 trial order and the 2020 typical edition. The 2020 typical edition is now acquired: its own decree (No. 31, 17 February 2020) cites a recognition letter of 21 November 2019 and makes the edition effective on 5 April 2020.
uses.limit: No complete collation of any two states. The 1773, 1936, 1971, 1982 and 2006 books, the Saigh 1936 booklet and the 2023 faithful's book were not acquired. Holdings-catalogue leads from the reviewer's Najm al-Mashriq reading remain unresolved identities, not versions.
next_sources: Moussess, 'Les huit éditions du missel chaldéen', POC 1 (1951) 209–220
Delly, 'L'édition du Missel chaldéen de 1901', OCP 23 (1957) 159–170
uses.review_remaining_gap: No two states collated; 1773, 1936, 1971, 1982 and 2006 books unacquired; 1936 differs from 1901 in at least two readings; Moussess 1951/1954/1955 and Delly 1957 unread; Arabic-section holdings unbucketed.

uses.label: Earlier Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry before and beside the Catholic line)
uses.finding: Macomber 1966 lists dated witnesses of the Apostles' anaphora from the twelfth century onward and groups those from about 1570 into three traditions: Alqosh, Chaldean and Malabar. Vatican Syriac 42 (1603) and Borgia Syriac 150 (sixteenth century) are now acquired as complete image sets.
uses.limit: Shared heritage is not Catholic reception. No manuscript was collated here.
next_sources: Macomber, 'A List of the Known Manuscripts of the Chaldean Hudra', OCP 36 (1970) 120–134
Webb, 'Variations dans les versions manuscrites de la liturgie nestorienne d'Addai et de Mari', Sacris Erudiri 18 (1967–68) 478–523
uses.review_remaining_gap: Theodore and Nestorius manuscript traditions (Vadakkel 1989, Naduthadam 1992), Gelston 1992, Macomber 1970 Hudra list and Webb 1967–68 unread; Macomber witnesses outside the traditions (a Khoshaba ritual 1664, w Berlin 41 1834, z McHardy codex 1908) and L Saigh hudra unlabelled; several Desreumaux ranges dropped.

uses.label: Assyrian Church of the East and the Anglican Urmia mission books (collateral, not Catholic)
uses.finding: The Urmia 1889 lectionary table and the Urmia 1890 Liturgy of the Apostles were printed by the Archbishop of Canterbury's mission (title page and catalogue). Kelaita's Mosul 1928 Taksa is the Church of the East edition Macomber cites as Ke. None is linked to Chaldean Catholic reception.
uses.limit: No reception evidence links these books to the Chaldean Catholic Church.
next_sources: Kelaita, The Liturgy of the Church of the East (Mosul 1928) original
uses.review_remaining_gap: Kelaita 1928 and its reported 1959 reissue unacquired; the Urmia second part (1891–1892) unidentified; Sako's Bedjan 1890 Urmia printing unresolved.

uses.label: Malabar manuscript tradition (routed to the malabar lane)
uses.finding: Macomber assigns Borgia Syriac 36 (seventeenth or eighteenth century) to the Malabar tradition; it is acquired here because the prior researcher started it, and is labelled for the malabar lane.
uses.limit: No Chaldean reception is claimed for Malabar witnesses.
next_sources: Malabar lane's cold review of Vatican Syriac 66 and Borgia Syriac 36
uses.review_remaining_gap: Borg. sir. 36 coverage moved to the Syro-Malabar row; Z and Vat. sir. 66 belong to the malabar lane.

uses.label: Chaldean Eparchy of St Peter the Apostle (San Diego) local use of the 2007 reform
uses.finding: Jammo's 2006 account and Sako's 2025 account agree that the reformed text was used in St Peter's eparchy; a 2013 Syriac Taksa from that eparchy is offered only as a five-page excerpt.
uses.limit: The full 2013 book and its approval are not seen.
next_sources: Full 2013 Syriac Taksa of the Eparchy of St Peter the Apostle
uses.review_remaining_gap: Whole 2013 book, its approval and its relation to the 2006 approved book unseen.

uses.label: Local use of Amadiya and Shamkan (catalogue lead)
uses.finding: The reviewer read a Najm al-Mashriq holding (T/404/9, catalogued 2002) titled for this local use.
uses.limit: Original book unseen; local title does not prove a distinct recension.

searches.repository: Web discovery (prior researcher's tool, log calls 19–49)
searches.outcome: Leads: Thalassery list of printed Taksas (1767, 1773, 1876, 1890, 1901, 1906, 1928, 1936), Mando's 2012 book list, Sako 2025 (MECC copy), the St Peter parish 2020 PDFs and the Addai congress bibliographies.
searches.extent_examined: Result snippets and opened pages recorded in the log digest; snippets are leads only.
searches.unexamined_range: No search reached an original 1773, 1936, 1971 or 2006 book.

searches.outcome: Six complete PDFs acquired (1876, 1889, 1890 and the three 1900 lection volumes). Direct HTML list and title pages now return a browser-script proof-of-work challenge or an empty list ('Keine Einträge vorhanden'); the OAI-PMH MODS endpoint returned full records.

searches.unexamined_range: The 254-title Syrian group list was read only through the prior web tool's rendered view (titles 101–200 page); offsets 1–100 and 201–254 were not captured as bytes.

searches.repository: Digital Vatican Library IIIF and OPAC
searches.outcome: Six manifests and all 1,526 page images acquired; Vat. sir. 43 and 83 have no IIIF manifest (HTTP 404). OPAC records cite Macomber 1966 and Webb 1967–68 for all six.
searches.extent_examined: Manifests, OPAC bibliography lists and the shelfmark target or first leaf of each image set.
searches.unexamined_range: Folio-level identification of the anaphora in each image set; Vatican Syriac manuscripts outside these six.

searches.repository: Assemani, Bibliothecae Apostolicae Vaticanae codicum manuscriptorum catalogus I.2 (1758), Internet Archive OCR
searches.outcome: Entries XLII, XLIII and XLIV read (OCR lines 20476–20960): XLII (1603, Gazarta) has the Apostles' liturgy at f. 25v without the words of institution; XLIII (Rome, August 1701, Patriarch Joseph of Amid) adds the words of institution on a slip from the Maronite Missal (Rome 1592) at f. 29 and the Johannine last Gospel; XLIV (same hand) writes the words of institution at f. 28v under a rubric.
searches.extent_examined: Three catalogue entries read in OCR; the page images were not checked.
searches.unexamined_range: The rest of the volume; codices after the Assemani series (303, 491) and the Borgia fund.

searches.outcome: Every direct request returned a browser-script challenge or HTTP 403.
searches.unexamined_range: All syri.ac descriptions of these shelfmarks.

searches.outcome: Python urllib received HTTP 403; curl succeeds. searches.extent_examined: HTTP headers of the three files; the whole 03 file.
searches.unexamined_range: Contents of the 01 Sureth and 04 English files (deferred translations).

versions.label: British Library Add. 14669 ff. 20–21, anaphora fragments
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Fragmentary witness; Connolly's edition (1925) and both bibliographic controls class it as East Syrian. A scholarly attribution, not Chaldean reception.
versions.unresolved: Connolly's edition and the manuscript were not read.

versions.label: Reported seventh-century ordering of the anaphoras under Ishoʿyahb III
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Literary testimony reported by Sako 2025; no book or manuscript state attests it.
versions.unresolved: Not a book state; no date bounds assigned.

versions.label: Mosul, Mar Eshaya Hudra (Macomber's base text): Apostles' anaphora
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Oldest written state in the dossier (stage chaldean-east-syriac:mar-eshaya): no written private prayers and no institution narrative.
versions.unresolved: Manuscript images registered at HMML/CNMO are not accessible without registration.

versions.label: Diarbekir Hudra (Macomber A), surviving volume
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Writes the private prayers absent from Mar Eshaya (dossier transition written-kushshaphe).

versions.label: Mardin 22 Hudra (Macomber B)
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Dated witness still without the private prayers; not a reform.

versions.label: Fifteenth- and sixteenth-century witnesses before the three traditions (Macomber C–Q)
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Witnesses Macomber does not assign to a tradition; grouped, not counted as versions.
versions.unresolved: Individual identities beyond the Vatican items are unverified.

versions.label: Vatican, Borg. sir. 150 (Macomber N)
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Pre-family witness; OPAC also cites Macomber's Hudra list (1970), so it may be a Hudra.
versions.unresolved: Folio of the anaphora and the manuscript's genre not identified on the images.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 42 (Macomber W): Order of Priests with the Apostles and Nestorius
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Copied at Gazarta; the Apostles' liturgy (f. 25v) lacks the words of institution (Assemani). Came from the library of Patriarch Joseph I (BYU description card, image 1).
versions.unresolved: Colophon not read on the image; the BYU card's '165 folios' and 'completed in 1202' differ from Assemani's 169 folios and 1603.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 303 (Macomber Y, Alqosh tradition)
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Member of Macomber's Alqosh tradition.
versions.unresolved: Colophon and anaphora folio not identified.

versions.label: Alqosh manuscript tradition (Macomber AQ: R 1570 to u 18th/19th c.)
versions.tradition_or_use: Church of the East manuscript heritage (shared ancestry)
versions.distinctness_basis: Textual tradition defined by Macomber; a layer, not one version.
versions.unresolved: Members other than Vat. sir. 303 not acquired.

versions.label: Chaldean manuscript tradition (Macomber CH: f 1686 to y 1850)
versions.distinctness_basis: Macomber's Chaldean tradition (f, g, h, l, m, o, q, r, x, y), the manuscript layer of the Catholic line; includes the Vatican items 491, 44 and 43.
versions.unresolved: Members outside the Vatican not acquired.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 491 (Macomber f, Chaldean tradition)
versions.distinctness_basis: Earliest dated member of Macomber's Chaldean tradition.
versions.unresolved: Colophon and anaphora not located on the images.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 44 (Macomber h): baptism, Apostles' liturgy and Arabic Gospel lections
versions.date_label: 1691 (Macomber); hand of Patriarch Joseph of Amid (Assemani)
versions.distinctness_basis: Writes the words of institution in the Apostles' liturgy at f. 28v under a rubric (Assemani), a Catholic supplement absent from Vat. sir. 42.
versions.unresolved: f. 28v not checked on the image; the 1691 date is Macomber's and Assemani gives no year.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 43 (Macomber l): Missal with Pontifical, copied at Rome by Patriarch Joseph I
versions.distinctness_basis: Assemani reports the words of institution supplied on a slip taken from the Maronite Missal (Rome 1592) and the Johannine last Gospel added after the liturgy: concrete Latinizing changes.
versions.unresolved: Not digitized (IIIF manifest HTTP 404; OPAC shows no digitization); images unavailable.

versions.label: Chaldean Patriarchate MS 38 (Macomber i, 1697) and Renaudot's reported Joseph I witness of 1697
versions.distinctness_basis: Macomber places Chald. Patr. 38 in the Alqosh tradition; the dossier's Renaudot lead (Joseph I, 1697) is not shown to be the same book.

versions.label: Vatican, Borg. sir. 36 (Macomber k, Malabar tradition)
versions.distinctness_basis: Malabar tradition witness; no Chaldean reception claimed.

versions.label: Vatican, Vat. sir. 66 (Macomber O), Malabar-associated codex
versions.date_label: main codex 1529; ownership note 1545; added leaves undated
versions.distinctness_basis: Reviewer and malabar cold reading of Assemani; the anaphora sits in an added tail.
versions.unresolved: Owned by the malabar lane; not acquired here.
